originalCi.test: two parallel installs recover the same stale lock and preserve both inventory items
originalCi.failure: Both processes exited successfully but inventory omitted the second item.

diagnosis.cause: Inventory acquisition called proper-lockfile without serializing stale recovery. Two stale stat snapshots allow the later rmdir to delete the first contender replacement lock.
diagnosis.deterministicMethod: Two real subprocesses pause callbacks after reading the same stale lock stat. The first enters inventory mutation and waits before commit; the second resumes its stale callback while the first remains inside. Filesystem reads, deletion, lock creation and inventory commits are real.
diagnosis.beforeFix: The second process entered the critical section before the first released its lock.
diagnosis.afterFix: The second contender waits outside stale recovery, observes the fresh replacement lock, enters only after release, and both inventory items persist.

change.mechanism: Reuse the existing PID and nonce acquisition gate for inventory lock acquisition only.
change.retryBoundary: The remaining budget is passed to proper-lockfile maxRetryTime; an already scheduled retry can add up to the existing 1000 ms maximum polling interval, excluding filesystem scheduling delays.
change.timeoutCleanup: Remove only the current contender files, retain the live owner, and permit normal acquisition after the owner disappears.
change.targetGateDefault: Unchanged; optional timeout is supplied only by inventory.
unchanged: inventory critical section and commit checks

verification.testedState: Working-tree fix based on the original CI commit; not a remote macOS result.

limits: The corrected candidate still requires remote macOS CI verification.
The plugin must be rebuilt to embed the corrected shared core.
An older CLI that does not participate in the acquisition gate can still perform unsafe concurrent stale recovery; mixed old and corrected processes are not covered.
This evidence does not resolve the independent DSH root session-adapter restart defect.
